clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with a 5-year history of intermittent erythematous, granulomatous, discoid plaques on his trunk, arms, and back, associated with normocytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated inflammatory markers. Initial skin biopsy (E002) showed a superficial dermal inflammatory infiltrate of histiocyte-like cells and scattered neutrophils with differential considerations including Sweet's syndrome and interstitial granulomatous dermatitis. A subsequent skin biopsy (E004) demonstrated similar features with prominent papillary dermal edema and was confirmed by specialist hematopathology as histiocytoid Sweet's syndrome. Subsequent genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in the UBA1 gene with a variant allele frequency of 27.7% (E006), confirming VEXAS syndrome. Following diagnosis, he was placed on long-term prednisolone therapy (E007), with complete clearance of the rash, resolution of shoulder pain, and no further flares reported.
